sourceTitle: How Banks Create Money From Nothing
title: Banks Don't Lend Your Deposits — They Create Money
hook: Banks do not lend out your deposits. They create the money.
question: Did you know that?

scenes.narration: Here is something almost nobody is actually taught in school. Banks do not lend out your savings. They create brand-new money whenever they make a loan.
When a bank approves your loan, it simply types the amount into your account. The loan creates the deposit, not the other way around.
This is not a conspiracy theory. It is standard, textbook economics.
Astonishingly, around ninety-seven percent of all money is created this way by private banks, not printed by the government.
That lending is what makes up most of the money supply held by the public.
It all works because banks keep only a small fraction of deposits in reserve.
Take out a three hundred thousand dollar mortgage, and that money quite literally appears out of nothing.
So, did you actually know that is how money really works?
